create_refinery_n_reactors.ponder.shared: Cascading gas centrifuges
Place one two-block-tall centrifuge and drive its bottom shaft at 32 RPM or more. Each machine uses 32 SU per RPM.
Feed enters the lower side faces only. It cannot be extracted through the inlet.
Extract the primary product from the upper top face with a Create pump and pipe.
Extract the separated tails from the upper side faces. Keep both product outlets clear.
Adjacent machines join through their upper headers; drive each bottom shaft independently. Water needs two powered stages and uranium enrichment needs four.
Compact fuel needs eight powered stages. Speed increases with powered stages, up to four times; a cascade contains at most sixteen machines.
Stopped machines do not count as powered stages. Check stages and stop reasons with goggles or a Display Link.
Pressing synthetic diamonds
Place the press above a Blaze Burner and feed it a Blaze Cake for superheat. Ordinary kindled heat cannot run this process.
Drive either shaft face at 64 RPM or more. The press uses 256 SU per RPM.
Insert graphite and nickel with funnels, chutes or arms from above or the sides without a shaft. Iron also works, but is slower.
Six anvils compress the glowing sample into a diamond. Returned catalyst goes back into its input slot; the output slot holds diamonds only.
Losing heat or speed pauses the paid batch without resetting progress. Clear a full output to resume.

create_refinery_n_reactors.ponder.shared: Reaction tower
Stack reaction towers 3x3 and three to twelve layers high. Like a lidded vessel, the tower is hollow inside its walls. The ladder is at the far end of the left wall as you face the tower.
Use catalyst baskets on the open hatch. One drops into each layer, from the bottom up.

Put the same catalyst into every basket through the hatch, or with a funnel on top, then close the hatch to run. The catalyst decides the reaction; baskets without catalyst run reactions that need none.
Pipe the feed into a side of the bottom layer. The gas rises along the shell and flows down through the beds from the top. Both feeds of a reaction may share one pipe.
Products leave from another side of the bottom layer, or from the middle of its underside.
Blaze burners under the base give the heat a reaction needs. No rotation is needed.

Without catalyst baskets the reaction tower is a high-pressure gas-liquid separator. Each layer runs one batch at a time.
Pipe the mixture into a side of the bottom layer, such as cooled synthesis gas from the ammonia loop.
The liquid collects at the bottom and leaves from a side of the bottom layer.
The gas leaves from a side of the top layer.
While it separates, the sight glasses in the middle of each side open, showing the liquid level inside.

On the front, the side that faced you as you placed it, each layer with a basket shows its temperature on the left. The gauge on the right, second from the bottom, shows the loop pressure: 15 to 25 MPa.
Fresh catalyst reacts mostly in the upper layers, which run hottest. As the catalyst wears, the upper layers stay cooler and the heat moves down into the lower ones.
Mix and transport liquids and gases
Build an ordinary lidded vessel without internal parts. Feed different liquids through its normal side connections.
In the tank, heavier liquids settle below lighter ones. The window shows each layer in its own colour.

A machine takes only the gases it uses out of a gas mixture and lets the others out of its gas outlet unchanged. The gases a machine makes leave together as one mixture, in proportion to their amounts.
Use normal Create pipes, pumps and tanks. Splitting a flow keeps each constituent without losing millibuckets, and each constituent still needs suitable pipe and tank materials.
Hover a fluid container or JEI fluid to see its composition. Pure fluids and solutions with one known solute show a rotating model. A Display Link lists mixture amounts.

Wet leaching and slow clarification
Use a lidded vessel with stirred internals and heating below. No dedicated leaching tank is needed.
Feed crushed iron, copper, zinc or tin through a funnel into the lidded vessel. Gold has no chemical route.
Supply dilute sulfuric acid to a lower liquid port and compressed air or oxygen to an upper gas process port.
Heat and stir: 3 crushed ores + 750 mB acid + 250 mB oxidant produce 4000 mB slurry in the lidded vessel.
Build an odd circular tank from tank casings. Place the center drive at rim height and replace the center floor block with a downward-facing inlet.
Pump slurry into the left wall or the bottom feed. Use acid-resistant piping for leach slurry.
Use a funnel at the opposite wall to load flocculant. One item halves a 200-tick batch.
Reduce the center drive to 1–4 RPM. Per 1000 mB slurry, collect 750 mB clear solution at the rim and two tailings mud below.
At 5–16 RPM, suspended dirt carries into the overflow and raises the next electrowinning batch’s work, up to twice normal. At 17 RPM or above, the same slurry simply overflows without separation.
At zero RPM, settling still works but mud cannot leave. The underflow fills and stops further processing until the scraper runs again.

Send clear solution to the electrolysis cells: each 1000 mB returns 3 ingots and 250 mB acid. For 3 ores, this line yields 9 ingots and recycles 750 mB acid. Press tailings mud for clay and sand; heated mixing also recovers occasional quartz.
Choosing a pipe for the fluid
Standard copper pipes carry liquids at atmospheric pressure, from ambient to hot. Gases can use any pipe material.
Start with fired ceramic pipe for acidic liquids. It handles hot acid at atmospheric pressure.
Reinforced pipe carries very-hot pressurised liquids. It is not acid resistant.
Stainless pipe carries hot, high-pressure and acidic liquids. Wrench it for a window or add casing.
Nickel-alloy pipe resists fluorides. Look at a pipe with goggles to see its liquid ratings.
Zirconium pipe carries hot acids as well as high-grade heat and pressure.
Use insulated pipe for cryogenic liquids, such as liquid helium.
Liquids outside the pipe ratings stay at the source. Gas retains its grade in transit.
Choosing a tank for the fluid
Choose tanks by temperature, pressure and corrosion grades. Incompatible fluids stay outside; tanks do not rupture.
Stainless tanks store acid-resistant liquids, through very hot and pressurised grades. They reject all gases and fluorides.
Use cryogenic tanks for liquefied gases. They accept cryogenic through ambient grades.
Pressure tanks store liquids through hot and high-pressure grades. Gas and corrosive fluids are rejected.

Store gases only in damping tubes, gas containers or the gas holder. Liquid tanks, including stainless, pressure and cryogenic tanks, reject gases. Dedicated machine gas ports still accept their process gases.
Gas holders store the atmospheric volume; damping tubes and gas containers use the high-pressure storage ratio of 64. Liquid tanks do not gain gas capacity.
Goggles show the accepted grades and corrosion resistance. After a refused insertion, check the rejection reason there.
Pressure, the basics
Fluid pressure has three grades: atmospheric, pressurised and high pressure.
Check the accepted grades on pipes and tanks with goggles.
A Create pump moves both gases and liquids.
A compressor raises supported fluids by one pressure grade.
Heating follows the recipe heat requirement. It does not build an adjustable tank pressure.
Higher-rated tanks hold more gas in the same volume. Liquid capacity stays unchanged.
A reducing valve lowers supported fluids by one grade. Other fluids pass unchanged.
Match materials to grades and corrosion. Mismatches are rejected without leaks or rupture.

For parts that need pure chromium, use thermite with aluminium in a superheated stainless impeller vessel. Recover chromium, iron and alumina.
%s → %s

Pure chromium also makes stainless steel. The steel family also shows the converter route.

book.create_refinery_n_reactors.manual.p:
Refinery 'n' Reactors
Plant Manual

Build plants with Create's machines that give you more metal from every ore, far more rotation, faster farms, mining charges and goods to sell.

Contents

1 Looking things up
2 First: steel, stainless, vessel
3 More metal from ores
4 More rotation
5 Faster farms
6 Mining charges
7 Selling products
8 Better materials
9 Grades and pipes
10 When it stops

1 Looking things up

Hold a part and press W to open its Ponder, a moving guide.
JEI shows every recipe and its amounts.
Look at a running machine with Create's goggles to see its grades and why it stopped.

Your path

The advancement screen (L) has this mod's path. Each one you earn says what it gives you and the next step.

First set up Create's basics: rotation, a blaze burner, a basin with a mixer, and a press.

2 First: steel

Crush coal or charcoal into carbon powder.
Superheat 4 iron ingots + 1 carbon powder under a mixer: 4 steel workpieces.
Press each five times: 4 steel ingots in total.

Stainless steel

All in a basin. Heat 2 pentlandite: nickel oxide. Superheat it with carbon powder: nickel. Superheat 2 chromite and 1 carbon powder: ferrochrome.
Superheat 6 iron, 2 ferrochrome, 1 nickel: 10 stainless.

The lidded vessel

Make it from stainless steel plates, an iron trapdoor and a basin. Set 3 x 3, stack 1 to 4 high, put a stirrer in each layer, turn the bottom centre at 32 RPM and heat from below.

Fluids go in and out by pipe, solids by funnel. Keep the hatch closed.
Look the vessel up in JEI to see what it makes.

Ponder: Building a stirred reactor

3 More metal from ores

Iron, copper, zinc, tin; no gold.
At 64 RPM, a large leaching tank mixes 3 crushed ores + 750 mB dilute acid + 250 mB compressed air or oxygen into 4000 mB slurry.

Clarify and recover

1–4 RPM: 1000 mB slurry gives 750 mB solution + 2 mud.
Electrolysis: 1000 mB solution gives 3 ingots + 250 mB acid for 20 kJ. Dirt raises this work.
Ponder: Wet processing

Hydrogen

Power comes from Create: Electro Energetics generators and wires.
Cells, electrode heads and a controller split water into H2 and O2.

Ponder: Making hydrogen by water electrolysis

Sulfuric acid

Burn sulfur in a heated vessel with air from an open pipe end. Stir the gas into water with air and an iron nugget: dilute acid, no power.
Use ceramic pipe.
Ponder: From sulfur and recovered gas to sulfuric acid

4 More rotation

Goal: per blaze burner, turbines give up to twice a steam engine's rotation.
A horizontal tank over burners makes high-pressure steam when heated, superheated when superheated.
Refined diesel also runs diesel engines.

Feed the high-pressure turbine, pump its exhaust to the low-pressure one, and cool that with a condenser.
RBMK gives far more steam: uranium, enrichment, pellets, fuel rods. Fusion irradiates cartridges into netherite scrap.

5 Faster farms

Goal: one fertilizer grows the 3 x 3 crops around the one you use it on; deployers spread it too.
Compress air, separate nitrogen, make ammonia, then nitric acid and ammonium nitrate.

Ammonium nitrate grows each crop as far as two bone meals; ammonium sulfate as far as one.

Ponder: From ammonia to nitric acid and fertilizers

6 Mining charges

Goal: dig wide areas without a pickaxe.
Mix ammonium nitrate with diesel into ANFO and craft blasting charges. A quarry drive digs a marker's area; its side belt brings the ore back to the drive.

7 Selling products

Goal: emeralds and experience.
Attach the dispatch docket to a Create item vault. It orders fuel, alloys, rubber, fertilizer, building materials and plastics; full cargo is paid for.
Ponder: Deliver industrial products

8 Better materials

Six new ores give metals for tougher pipes and tanks. Crush them first; each metal has its own Ponder.
Molybdenum: roast with oxygen, reduce with hydrogen; nickel can be made this way too.

Aluminium, titanium, zirconium: dissolve in acid to an oxide, then use the molten salt electrolysis furnace. Make zirconia first: the furnace needs it.
Pure chromium: thermite with aluminium.
Oil: preheat crude, split it in a 2 x 2 column, crack naphtha, polymerise ethylene and press plastic sheets for gaskets.

9 Grades and pipes

Choose pipes and tanks by heat grade, pressure grade and corrosion resistance. Incompatible fluids are refused. Pumps also move gases.
Ponder: Pressure, the basics

10 When it stops

Look at it with goggles: they say why. Common causes:
- an outlet is full
- not hot enough or not turning fast enough
- a hatch is open
- wrong amounts (check JEI)

Run the downward-facing fan above the duct at 32 RPM or faster. Pump recovered steam out through the round nozzle.
Steam mist dissipates much faster under a clear sky.

Charge them with external rotation first.

Extend the complete cell in three-block increments, keeping the same width and height.
Each added cell needs its own fan, eight shrouds and driven column.
